questions.question: The fifteenth day of the month of June is a Saturday. What will be the last day of the next month which has 31 days?
questions.solution:
The fifteenth day of the month of June is a Saturday.

Saturday falls on these dates:

15 + 7 = 22

22 + 7 = 29

And the last day of June, i.e, 30 June is Sunday.

And 1st of July will be Monday.

Monday falls on these dates:

1 + 7 = 8

8 + 7 = 15

15 + 7 = 22

22 + 7 = 29

30th is Tuesday and 31st is Wednesday.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Wednesday"**.

Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the @ signs and to balance the given equation.

72 @ 9 @3 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6
questions.solution:

Given:

⇒ 72 @ 9 @3 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6

(1) ÷, ×, +, =, -, +

⇒ 72 @ 9 @3 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6

After putting the signs:

⇒ __**72 ÷ 9**__ × 3 + 6 = 6 - 6 + 6

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 8 × 3 + 6 = 12 - 6

⇒ 24 + 6 = 6

⇒ 30 = 6

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

(2) **÷, ×, +, =, ×, -**

⇒ 72 @ 9 @3 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6

After putting the signs:

⇒** __72 ÷ 9__** × 3 + 6 = __**6 × 6**__ - 6

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ __**8 × 3**__ + 6 = 36 - 6

⇒ 24 + 6 = 30

⇒ **30 = 30**

Here, the equation is **satisfied.**

(3) ×, ÷, =, -, +, ×

⇒ 72 @ 9 @3 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6

After putting the signs:

⇒ 72 × __**9 ÷ 3**__ = 6 - 6 + __**6 × 6**__

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ __**72 × 3**__ = 6 - 6 + 36

⇒ 216 = 42 - 6

⇒ 216 = 36

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

(4) +. ×, =, -, ÷, +

⇒ 72 @ 9 @3 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6 @ 6

After putting the signs:

⇒ 72 + __**9 × 3**__ = 6 - __**6 ÷ 6**__ + 6

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 72 + 27 = 6 - 1 + 6

⇒ 99 = 12 - 1

⇒ 99 = 11

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (2)".

• The Natya Shastra covers a wide range of topics related to** dance, music, and theater,** including the classification of dance forms, the elements of performance, and the roles of the performer and the audience.

• **Dharma Shastra is a collection of religious and ethical guidelines for Hindus.**
 
 
• These texts are based on **Puranas. **

questions.question: Which tunnel has been built with ultra-modern specifications in the Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas at an altitude of 3000 meters above Mean Sea Level?
questions.solution:

• The tunnel is named after former Prime Minister of India, **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, who initiated the project in** 2002** and inaugurated it in **2020.**
 
• The tunnel connects Manali to **Lahaul-Spiti Valley** throughout the year and reduces the distance between the two regions by about** 46 km.**

• **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel is also known as the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel.**
 
 
• It is a **9.28 km **long road tunnel on the National Highway 44 in **Jammu and Kashmir,** India.
 
• It is located at an altitude of **1,200 meters** and connects **Chenani **with** Nashri.**
 
 
 
• **Bhatan Tunnel is a 1.6 km long railway tunnel on the Konkan Railway route in Maharashtra, India.**
 
 
• It is located at an altitude of **70 meters** and connects the villages of **Bhatan and Kamathe.**

questions.question: Identify the element that does NOT belong to Period 6 of the Modern Periodic Table.

• **Silicon** belongs to** Period 3** of the Periodic Table and is not part of Period 6.
 
• **Tungsten** (atomic number 74), **Rhenium **(atomic number 75), and **Platinum **(atomic number 78) all belong to **Period 6** of the Periodic Table.
 
• **Tungsten is a transition metal that is commonly used in the manufacture of electrical contacts, filaments, and X-ray tubes.**
 
• Rhenium is a rare and expensive metal that is used in high-temperature superalloys, as well as in the manufacture of electrical contacts and filaments.
 
• **Platinum is a precious metal that is used in jewelry, as well as in the manufacture of catalytic converters, electrical contacts, and laboratory equipment.**

• Its atomic number is **14** and its symbol is** Si.**
 
• **It has a blue-grey metallic sheen and is a hard, brittle crystalline solid.**
 
• **It is a semiconductor and tetravalent metalloid.**
 
• It belongs to the periodic table's **group 14.**

questions.question: From which country were the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ireland.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which was adopted in 1937.**
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are a set of guidelines for the government to frame policies and laws that promote the welfare of the people and establish a just and egalitarian society.
 
• **They are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of Ireland also includes a set of** Directive Principles**, which are similar in nature to those of India.

 
 
• However, the Irish Constitution also includes Fundamental Rights that are justifiable, unlike the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• The US Constitution does not have Directive Principles, but it does have a Bill of Rights that guarantees certain fundamental rights to its citizens.

• The function of glycolipids embedded in the outer lipid layer is comparable.

questions.question: In a 200-m linear race, if A gives B a start of 25 m, then A wins the race by 10 seconds. Alternatively, if A gives B a start of 45 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does A take to run 200m?

**Given**

In a 200-m linear race, if A gives B a start of 25 m, then A wins the race by 10 seconds.

**Formula used**

Distance = speed × time

**Calculation **

Let’s assume speed of A as vₐ and speed of B as vb

Then, in a 200 M race distance run by A = 200 m

Distance run by B after getting head start of 25 M = 175 m

Time taken by A = 200/vₐ

Time taken by B = 175/vb

Since B lacks behind by 10 sec therefore Time taken by B is more as compare to that of A by 10 sec,

⇒ 175/vb - 200/vₐ = 10 ....(1)

if A gives B a start of 45 m, the race ends in a dead heat,

Time taken by B = (200 - 45)/vb = 155/vb

Time taken by A = 200/vₐ

Both finish at same time,

∴ 155/vb = 200/vₐ

⇒ vₐ = 40/31 × vb ----(2)

Putting (2) in (1) we get,

Vb = 2 

Time taken by B to complete 200M race would be 175 / 2 = 87.5 seconds

Thus time taken by A would be = 87.5 - 10 = 77.5 second

**A takes 77.5 seconds to run 200m.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

In the second case:

Time taken by B to run 155m = time taken by A to run 200m = x s

From the first and second cases, it is clear that for (175-155)m = 20m extra run B takes 10 s extra time.

Thus speed of B = 20m/10s = 2m/s

**Therefore, Time taken by A to run 200m = Time taken by B to run 155m = 155/2 = 77.5 s**
